The P&L 'Share-based compensation' line inside non-interest expense (C$666M 9M-FY26, C$1,002M FY25; RY_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt:460) is mostly cash-settled share units already expensed and hedged, so it is inside adjusted NIE and must not be charged again. Equity-settled issuance was 1.39M shares in 9M-FY26 (0.1% of count).
inputs.fx_note: CAD->USD 0.7019 (Yahoo CADUSD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-04T04:21Z). Parity check: TSX RY.TO C$278.91 x 0.7019 = US$195.77 vs NYSE RY US$195.67 (0.05% gap); one NYSE share = one TSX common share. Flows, cost of equity and equity bridge are CAD; the unsuffixed intrinsic values are converted to USD for comparison with the NYSE quote.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API, NYSE RY)
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,384.554M common shares outstanding at 2026-07-31 (Q3-26 Report to Shareholders Table 1) + 3.65M dilutive (Q3 average diluted 1,391.074M vs basic 1,387.423M) = 1,388.2M fully diluted. Held FLAT: equity-settled SBC is charged in the flows and buybacks (5.6M shares in Q3-26 at C$285.33; new NCIB for up to 45M shares to June 2027) are a use of the FCFE already being valued. buyback_cash is the Q3-26 quarter's C$1,603M (9M-FY26 C$4,236M).
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY in CAD, not a WACC: the flow is post-interest, post-preferred FCFE. Canada 10y ~3.4% + beta ~1.0-1.05 x 5.75% ERP = ~9.2-9.5%; base 9.5% (25bp below BMO's 9.75% for the lower beta and ~17-18% ROE franchise, above the ~9.2% CAPM point to stay inside the house bank range NAB.AX 9.7% / BMO 9.75% / USB 10.0%). Bull 9.25%; bear 10.0% (only +50bp because the bear credit path already carries most of the downside -- charge risk once).
inputs.lease_treatment: n/a -- bank; premises and lease cost are inside non-interest expense, no separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Preferred dividends + LRCN/AT1 distributions + NCI income (TTM C$565M = FY25 501 (20,369 - 19,868) less 9M-FY25 360 (14,935 - 14,575) plus 9M-FY26 424 (17,318 - 16,894)) are removed INSIDE the flow as a pre-tax equivalent (565 / (1 - 0.218) = C$722M), so the after-tax flow is adjusted net income to COMMON (TTM 22,534). Preferred shares and other equity instruments (C$11,114M at 2026-07-31; Q3-26 balance sheet) are therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (USB/BMO precedent; doing both charges them twice).
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (house precedent BMO, USB, TFC, HBAN, NTRS, STT, NAB.AX; SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book -- FCFE-at-CoE with retention = growth x regulatory capital is the equivalent flow form and keeps RY comparable with the other banks in this folder, in particular BMO valued the same day on the same mechanics). No prior RY valuation and no memory entry: first build. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = net interest income + non-interest income (RBC 'Total revenue'); 'ebitda' = adjusted pre-tax income + equity-settled SBC - pre-tax-equivalent(pref/AT1 distributions + NCI); D&A 0; 'capex' = capital retention needed to hold CET1 at a 13.0% run-rate as RWA grows with revenue = CET1/revenue 1.4213 x g/(1+g); wc 0; net_debt 0 (deposits C$1.64T, wholesale funding and the NVCC subordinated debentures are operating funding / regulatory capital, not acquisition debt). TTM BUILD (adjusted, C$M; Q4-FY25 = FY25 adjusted (Annual Table 16) less 9M-FY25 adjusted (Q3-26 non-GAAP table)): revenue 17,209 + 53,951 = 71,160; PCL 1,007 + 3,002 = 4,009 (5.6% of revenue, 0.37% of average loans -- slightly below through-cycle); adjusted NIE 9,221 + 28,383 = 37,604 (adjusted efficiency 52.8%); adjusted pre-tax 6,981 + 22,566 = 29,547 (ties: 71,160 - 4,009 - 37,604); adjusted tax 1,427 + 5,021 = 6,448 (21.8%); adjusted NI 5,554 + 17,545 = 23,099; adjusted NI to common 5,413 + 17,121 = 22,534. ADJUSTED, NOT REPORTED: the only remaining adjusting item is amortisation of acquisition-related intangibles (C$306M pre-tax 9M-FY26, ~C$410M TTM; ~C$300M after tax) -- non-cash, and goodwill (19,489) and intangibles (7,334) are already deducted from CET1; HSBC Canada integration costs ceased to be a specified item in Q3-FY25 and are inside adjusted NIE from then on. Reported TTM NI 22,752 vs adjusted 23,099 (1.5% gap). ebitda = 29,547 + 70 - 722 = 28,895 = 40.6% of revenue. CET1: 13.5% x RWA 777,987 = C$105.0B at 2026-07-31; the 13.0% run-rate (C$101.1B = 1.4213x TTM revenue) is the level RY has bought back down toward (13.5% average over 5 years, OSFI minimum 11.5% incl. 3.5% DSB); the ~50bp (~C$3.9B, ~C$2.80/share) held above the run-rate is NOT credited in the bridge -- a deliberate conservatism given rising GIL (0.91% vs 0.85%). last_fcf 16,813 = adjusted NI to common 22,534 less retention at the base year-1 growth of 6% (1.4213 x 0.06/1.06 x 71,160 = 5,721) -- an FCFE proxy, since bank OCF (C$+35.1B in Q3-26, -C$15.6B in Q2-24) is balance-sheet noise, not owner cash. MONERIS: RBC's 50% of the C$2B JV sale to Francisco Partners (announced 2026-08-10, closing by end Q1-FY27) books a ~C$475M after-tax gain (Q3-26 Note 15), credited in equity_bridge; the equity-accounted Moneris income lost from the flow is immaterial against C$22.5B and is not adjusted. FX: ~a third of earnings are USD/GBP/EUR-denominated (9M-FY26 translation -C$300M revenue), which partly hedges the CAD->USD conversion.

equity_bridge.item: Moneris Solutions 50% sale -- after-tax gain on closing
equity_bridge.note: Q3-26 Report to Shareholders, Note 15 / Corporate Events: ~C$2B cash consideration (RBC share 50%), estimated gain ~C$475M after tax (C$560M pre-tax), expected to close by end of Q1 FY2027 subject to regulatory approval. Credited because it is distributable CET1 that the TTM earnings flow does not contain; the carrying value of the JV is already in common equity. Subject to closing adjustments.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_3yr_cagr (book value per common share FY2022 72.85 -> FY2025 91.00 = 127,417 / 1,400.114M; FY2020 56.75; Q3-26 96.73). Matches management's 7%+ medium-term diluted-EPS objective; the 5yr BVPS CAGR of 9.9% runs from a COVID-provision FY2020 base and is not used.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3yr revenue CAGR 10.8% exceeds the 3yr BVPS CAGR 7.7% by ~40%: FY2022 revenue (48,985) was a trading/IB trough and the March-2024 HSBC Canada acquisition (~C$3-4B/yr revenue) is inorganic, so the 3yr revenue rate overstates organic growth. 5yr rates agree within 30% (revenue 7.1%, BVPS 9.9%, EPS 12.5%). The forward base path (6% -> 3%) is set below every historical rate.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_*_cagr fields carry REPORTED NET INCOME CAGRs (FY2022 15,794 / FY2020 11,432 -> FY2025 20,362): bank OCF/FCF swings with trading assets, deposits and securities and is not an owner cash flow. Adjusted NI FY2024 17,430 -> FY2025 20,870 (+20%); TTM adjusted 23,099. FY2025 BVPS 91.00 and FY2023 78.79 derived from Table 1 common equity / period-end shares (RY_Annual_FY2025.txt:156,163; RY_Annual_FY2023.txt:166,173) because the ten-year table did not extract; FY2020 and FY2022 read directly from the ten-year tables (RY_Annual_FY2020.txt:14217, RY_Annual_FY2022.txt:10810).

base.growth_rationale: TTM revenue +10.4% YoY (prior TTM 64,470) on a strong fee cycle (Wealth +12-16%, Capital Markets record) and HSBC Canada's last partial-year contribution; year 1 steps down to 6% (Canadian GDP ~1-1.5%, loan growth 2-4%, AUM growth on markets), tapering to 3% nominal by year 10. Below the 7%+ EPS objective because EPS growth also carries the buyback.
base.margin_rationale: FY0 40.6% = adjusted pre-tax 41.5% + SBC 0.1% - pref/NCI 1.0%. Base holds the adjusted efficiency ratio at ~52.5% -> 52.0% (management targets positive operating leverage; 52.8% TTM, 54.0% FY25) while PCL normalises from 0.37% to ~0.42% of loans (5.6% -> 6.5% of revenue), the two roughly offsetting: margin flat at 40.4-40.5%. Implied year-1 adjusted NI to common ~C$23.6B on ~C$136B average common equity = ~17.4% ROE -- at the 17%+ objective, not above it.
base.capex_rationale: Retention = CET1/revenue 1.4213 x g/(1+g): keeps CET1 at 13.0% as RWA grows with revenue.

bull.margin_rationale: Adjusted efficiency reaches ~50.5% by year 3 (AI/ATOM productivity, City National scale), PCL stays ~0.35% of loans (5.5% of revenue): 100 - 50.5 - 5.5 - 1.0 + 0.1 = 43.1%. Implied ROE ~19-20%.

bear.margin_rationale: Failed CUSMA review / broad U.S. tariffs tip Canada into recession in year 2: PCL rises to ~0.80% of loans (~C$8.9B, 12.4% of revenue -- the FY2020 COVID year was 0.63%, FY2009 0.72% on a smaller book) while revenue falls 1% (fee cycle turns, NIM compresses on BoC cuts) and efficiency slips to 55.5%: 100 - 55.5 - 12.4 - 1.0 + 0.1 = 31.2%. PCL 9% / efficiency 54.5% in year 3, then a recovery only to 38.8% (below today's 40.6%) because mortgage-renewal losses and City National CRE keep PCL ~0.45-0.50% and the efficiency programme stalls. Retention is held at 2.0% of revenue in the recession year rather than zero because credit migration inflates RWA even as revenue shrinks.
bear.capex_rationale: Same CET1/revenue 1.4213 x g/(1+g) formula; year-2 floor of 2.0% for RWA migration.

scenario_narratives.base: RBC compounds the franchise it already has: #1 Canadian retail/commercial share with HSBC Canada synergies fully in run-rate, Wealth Management (AUM C$1.7T) and Capital Markets growing with markets, City National returning to acceptable returns. Revenue growth 6% fading to 3%, adjusted efficiency ~52%, PCL normalising to ~0.42% of loans, ROE ~17-17.5% -- management's 17%+ objective met, not beaten. CET1 run at ~13% with the surplus returned through the 45M-share NCIB and a dividend growing with EPS (payout 40-50%).
scenario_narratives.bull: The fee cycle runs for several more years: Wealth and Capital Markets sustain double-digit revenue growth on buoyant markets and M&A, City National closes its ROE gap, AI-driven productivity takes adjusted efficiency to ~50%, and credit stays benign (PCL ~0.35%). ROE 19-20% and RBC keeps its premium among global peers; terminal multiple 15x FCFE.
scenario_narratives.bear: The CUSMA review fails or broad U.S. tariffs return; Canada enters recession in FY2027-28 with unemployment past 8%, mortgage renewals at higher rates and City National CRE/utilities losses push PCL to ~0.80% of loans, revenue falls as the fee cycle turns and NIM compresses. No solvency or funding case (CET1 13.5%, TLAC 30.9%, LCR 125%), but earnings power resets to a 38-39% pre-tax margin and the market re-rates RBC from a premium to a median Big Six multiple (11x FCFE).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Same 25/50/25 as BMO (valued the same day): the CUSMA review and tariff path are a near-term macro binary that RBC's own outlook names as the swing factor, Canadian unemployment is 6.4-6.9% and gross impaired loans are rising (0.91% vs 0.85%), so bear is held above the 15% default. Base 50%: Q3-26 (ROE 17.9%, record NI, efficiency 52.2%) is tracking the plan. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it requires the fee cycle to extend from what is already a record Wealth/Capital Markets quarter, with the stock at ~17x TTM adjusted EPS and ~2.9x book already discounting much of it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on what common shareholders can take out: adjusted net income to common less the earnings that must be retained to hold CET1 at ~13% as the balance sheet grows, discounted at the CAD cost of equity. Deposits and wholesale funding are operating funding, so there is no net-debt deduction; preferred/AT1 distributions and NCI are removed inside the flow. Flows and the bridge are in CAD; the per-share result is converted to USD at 0.7019 for comparison with the NYSE quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: PCL is 5.6% of revenue at 0.37% of loans, below through-cycle; a 0.80% year (bear) takes ~C$4.9B pre-tax out of one year's earnings and the model assumes it does not recur.
Fee-cycle peak: Wealth Management (+16% revenue YoY) and Capital Markets (record) are ~56% of segment net income; a reversal hits year-1 growth and margin directly.
Adjusted vs reported: the model uses adjusted earnings (acquisition-intangible amortisation only, ~C$300M after tax); the gap is small today but HSBC-style integration charges would widen it.
Capital run-rate: retention is set for 13.0% CET1; if OSFI raises the DSB or Basel floors bite, more earnings are retained and FCFE falls one-for-one.
FX: the CAD->USD conversion at 0.7019 moves the USD value one-for-one; roughly a third of earnings are foreign-currency, which partly hedges the translation.

Terminal value carries most of the value; the 14x FCFE cap (vs a 15.4x Gordon multiple at 9.5%/3%) and 3% CAD nominal terminal growth drive it. The stock's ~17x TTM adjusted P/E and ~2.9x P/B sit above what a 9.5% cost of equity supports.
